title: Basetwo, CPI, Labman and Nicoya run fed-batch bioreactors under autonomous AI feed control
summary: Four Canadian and UK organisations report closed-loop AI control of fed-batch bioreactors making a trastuzumab biosimilar candidate. Robotic sampling and a hybrid glucose model fed a predictive controller that set nutrient feeds without human input.

claims.text: Announced 11 Nov 2026 by Basetwo AI (Toronto) with CPI, Labman and Nicoya
Partners say autonomous control improved viability and titer versus manual control, which ran glucose-limited (company claim, no paper)
Works with existing process instrumentation; no extra spectroscopy needed (company claim)
Part of the 20-month BALANCE project funded by Innovate UK and NRC IRAP; Labman builds the automated aseptic sub-sampler, Nicoya the Alto SPR titer sensor

why_it_matters: Robot sampling plus fast at-line assays closing a loop; the same pattern applies to timed ADME sampling. Bioprocess, not discovery, and results are unpublished.

title: PyLabRobot weekend: PAA KX2 arm, Gyger CERTUS FLEX dispenser, Mantis v3 hardware
summary: PyLabRobot merged drivers for the PAA KX2 plate-handling arm and the Gyger CERTUS FLEX nanolitre valve dispenser, plus Mantis v3 arm, plate clamp and LC3 carousel control. A STAR reply-routing fix landed on 16 Nov.

claims.text: KX2 arm driver merged 14 Nov (PR #880), with a new CANopen transport in pylabrobot/io
CERTUS FLEX driver merged 15 Nov (PR #1637): a 1,237-line device module within 6,367 added lines, with recorded hardware replies as test fixtures
Mantis v3 arm initialisation, pneumatic plate clamp and calibrated LC3 carousel merged 16 Nov (PRs #1633-#1635)
ReplyRouter now drops unsolicited machine lines and never uses command id 0 (PR #1555)
Device registry lists 85 entries after these merges

why_it_matters: Nanolitre dispensing and plate movers are ADME-plate building blocks; open drivers for both lower the cost of a scripted, AI-drivable workcell.

title: Explainer: what 'hardware verified' means in PyLabRobot's CERTUS FLEX driver
summary: The driver's protocol notes list each operation with the test it got on one named dispenser, and say what was not tested. They state that command checks do not prove delivered volume; that needs measured valve calibration curves.

claims.text: Verified on one dispenser with firmware 1.0.7.378-trunk and an angled FLEX8 head; controller replies kept as regression fixtures
Talks to the controller directly over UDP (port 1964) or through the vendor INCO server over TCP (port 7979); no Windows DLL or SiLA needed
Dispense plans accept CSV volume maps, gradients and row/column/snake orders, with pause, resume and abort
Unverified: full travel envelope, other heads, cleaning effectiveness; volumes depend on supplied calibration

why_it_matters: A model for judging any AI-written driver: scoped evidence per command, honest gaps. Volume accuracy still needs a balance, as in any ADME assay qualification.

refs.title: PyLabRobot: CERTUS FLEX protocol and verification

title: Explainer: PyLabRobot drives the PAA KX2 arm over CANopen, not a vendor DLL
summary: The KX2 driver talks to the arm's motor drives over a CAN bus at 500 kbit/s through a new asynchronous CANopen transport. Setup records each drive's network state and restores it on teardown.

claims.text: Needs a CAN-USB adapter via python-can, e.g. SocketCAN can0 on Linux; no vendor DLL
Arm must expose CANopen nodes 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6; optional rail and gripper-less configurations unsupported
The transport serialises SDO transfers and refuses to release a channel while a cancelled transfer is still running
Optional barcode reader on a separate 9600-baud serial link

why_it_matters: Talking to the motor drives directly makes an arm scriptable from any OS; the restore-state rule protects shared pharma workcells.

title: Preprint: how optimiser repair rules behave in living-cell self-driving labs
summary: A bioRxiv simulation study tests repair rules for optimisers in living-cell self-driving labs with delayed, drifting readouts. Effects were small on rugged landscapes, and permanently retiring conditions hurt under noisy responses.

claims.text: Posted on bioRxiv in early November 2026 (doi 10.64898/2026.11.03.763926); not peer reviewed
Simulation only; no wet-lab run reported in the search abstract

why_it_matters: Cell assays (hepatocytes, Caco-2) drift; the lesson that hard-excluding conditions backfires under noise matters for any closed-loop cell work.
